column2: follow-up question (asked when this keyPoint is uncertain; must not contain the answer)
Two dogs of the same breed look alike. What do they share inside their cells that makes this so, and what must a parent cell do about it before dividing?
Why would copying all of a cell's instructions never give a perfect result every single time?
What does a population gain from its offspring being very like their parents when the surroundings stay the same?
Warm water arrives and most bacteria in a pond die. What would allow the pond to still have bacteria afterwards?
How does a single-celled organism make a new individual from itself, and how many does it make at a time in the simplest case?
What is different about how a malarial parasite divides compared with an amoeba, and how does a single-celled fungus used in baking differ again?
A pond alga's filament snaps into several parts. What can each part go on to become, and why does that work for such a simple body?
Why would cutting a cat's body into cells and letting each grow be a poor way for it to reproduce?
A flatworm is cut into several pieces and each becomes a whole worm. Which kind of cells make this possible, and why would you hesitate to call it normal reproduction?
Describe the stages from a small bump on a freshwater polyp's body to a separate individual, and where the bump forms.
A gardener plants a piece of stem and gets a whole new plant. Which parts of a plant can do this?
Why might a farmer prefer to grow banana plants this way rather than from seed, and what will the new plants be like compared with the parent?
How can a laboratory grow many identical, healthy plants starting from only a tiny bit of tissue?
On a mouldy bread slice, which structure makes the new mould and what keeps it safe until it can grow?
What do fission, budding, regeneration, vegetative propagation and spores all have in common about the number of parents?
If a cell copied its DNA with many more mistakes to get more variation, what would likely happen to the new cells?
Two parents each carry their own set of small differences. What does a child get that neither parent alone could produce?
If a sperm and an egg each carried a full set of chromosomes, how many would the child cell have, and what would happen over generations?
Why would it help one of the two germ-cells to be big and full of food while the other is small and able to move?
Name the male and female parts of a flower and say where the female germ-cell is found.
How would you tell a flower that has only one reproductive part from one that carries two kinds?
A bee carries yellow dust from one flower to the next. What is the name for what the bee has done, and what is it called if the dust lands on the flower it came from?
Once the pollen has reached the top of the pistil, how does its male cell travel down to the egg, and what is formed when they join?
What does the part that held the egg turn into after fertilisation, what does the part around it turn into, and what happens when the seed is given suitable conditions?
Name one change at around thirteen that happens to everyone, one that happens only to girls and one only to boys.
Why does the body wait until general growth is slowing down before the reproductive system matures?
Why are the organs that make male germ-cells kept outside the main body cavity, and which hormone do they release?
Trace the route of a sperm from where it is made until it leaves the body, and say what the glands along the way contribute.
When does a girl's body start releasing mature germ-cells, how often, and along which tube do they travel?
Where do the sperm and egg meet, and where does the resulting early cluster settle to keep growing?
A baby cannot eat or breathe in the womb. Through which structure does it get what it needs and get rid of waste, and why is that structure shaped as it is?
Each month the womb gets ready for a possible baby. What does it build up and why?
What happens to the prepared womb lining when no fertilisation takes place, and how long does this usually last?
Why does the body being sexually mature not settle whether someone should become sexually active, and what is one protection against infections?
Give three different ways pregnancy can be prevented and say what each does to stop it.
